question: to the Commission Liesbet Sommen (PPE), Martine Kemp (PPE), Wouter Beke (PPE), Pascal Arimont (PPE), Jana Toom (Renew), Paulo do Nascimento Cabral (PPE), Valérie Devaux (Renew), Maria Walsh (PPE), Verena Mertens (PPE), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Lena Schilling (Verts/ALE), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Danuše Nerudová (PPE), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Jutta Paulus (Verts/ALE), Gabriela Firea (S&D), Joanna Scheuring-Wielgus (S&D), Dennis Radtke (PPE), Hilde Vautmans (Renew), Benoit Cassart (Renew), Olivier Chastel (Renew) Subject:

France was recently shaken by a case of violent child sexual abuse that resulted in the victim’s death. The case exposed systemic failures and illustrates the need for a rapid, coordinated and victim-centred response to sexual violence. In Belgium, ten sexual assault centres provide an integrated model of care, offering medical, psychological and legal support under one roof, including emergency nursing care, case management and the possibility of a police interview at a single location. Such multidisciplinary centres can contribute to the earlier detection of sexual violence, improved collection of forensic evidence, and coordinated follow-up between healthcare and judicial services, thereby reducing the risk of further escalation and repeat victimisation. Directive (EU) 2024/1385 on combating violence against women and domestic violence1 requires Member States to provide victims of sexual violence with access to free medical and forensic examinations through coordinated support centres. The deadline for transposition is 14 June 2027. 1.
What steps is the Commission taking to provide Member States with guidance and resources for implementing Directive (EU) 2024/1385 by June 2027?
Which EU funding instruments can support the establishment of sexual assault centres, including facilities for minor victims?
